newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen metal futures Jan-May turnover up 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen metal futures Jan-May turnover up 50 pct.

text.p: Turnover on southern China's Shenzhen Mercantile Exchange, the nation's pioneering nonferrous metal futures exchange, rose nearly 50 percent year-on-year to 70 billion yuan ($8.4 billion) in the first five months of 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Tuesday.
"The turnover expansion was fuelled by active trading in aluminium and copper contracts," an exchange official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The volume of aluminium contracts reached 1.56 million tonnes in the January-May 1997 period, up 497.3 percent over the same period in 1996, the newspaper said.
Copper volume was up 9.98 percent to 1.70 million tonnes, it said.
Brokers attributed this to a relatively wide fluctuation in spot aluminium and copper prices on the international market this year, which increased trading interest.
Futures contracts listed on the Shenzhen Mercantile Exchange also included lead, zinc, tin and nickel but trading of these contracts had always been stagnant, the official said.
The exchange, set up in June 1991, has 204 members from across China, the newspaper said.
